rationale.conceptual: The method is an established, multi-part algorithm (liquid quench + REBO annealing + SED‑REBO relaxation + controlled tensile deformation with barostat/thermostat + bond-breaking analysis). It requires understanding of interatomic potentials, barostatting, and stress–strain conversion. The novelty lies in the PFC interpretation, but reproducing the fracture metrics essentially follows a documented protocol. This falls between a standard library call and a completely novel method, so conceptual = 3.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of at least two heavy stages: (1) generating the quenched and 25‑ns‑annealed models through multiple sequential MD runs with different settings, and (2) performing 10 tensile test simulations (5 per model) plus extracting and analyzing stress–strain curves and bond-breaking data. Setting up the custom liquid‑quench script, handling the external planar potential, and correctly converting engineering to true strain all add complexity. While the overall orchestration is not extremely fragile, it goes beyond a simple 2–3 step script, so execution = 3.

difficulty.reasoning: The core method is a series of standard molecular dynamics simulations (liquid quench, annealing, uniaxial tensile tests) using established interatomic potentials and analysis of bond-breaking events. It requires careful translation of the protocol into LAMMPS input files and post-processing to compute strain, stress, fracture energy, and PFC counts, but the underlying techniques are well-known in the field. The pipeline involves multiple stages (model generation, annealing, relaxation, tensile testing, analysis across ten runs) and thus presents a moderate engineering orchestration challenge.
